title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this part of the 'équation des lacets' notes, Grothendieck works with an abstract datum (𝔊, ρ, σ). Here 𝔊 is a (profinite) group, typically containing an index-2 subgroup 𝔊⁺. ρ and σ are distinguished elements playing the role of the order-6 and order-4 elliptic generators. They satisfy the 'loop equation' type relations (ρ³ = σ² central, etc.). From this datum he builds associated groups:
- normalisers/centralisers N_ρ, N_σ, N*_ρ, N*_σ, Z_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ};
- 'modular' groups S_0 M_{ρ,σ} and M_{ρ,σ}, which are subgroups of Aut or Out of 𝔊 preserving the data. These are analogues of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on the tower.

On the previous page (Grothendieck's p.589) he studies functoriality. For a surjective homomorphism φ: 𝔊 → 𝔊' compatible with the data, he gives conditions ('prolongeable') under which φ extends to φ_M: S_0 G^𝔊_{ρ,σ} → S_0 G^{𝔊'}_{ρ,σ}. He also gives a variant where condition (c) is required only on a subgroup Z^♮ ⊂ Z_{ρ,σ}, producing groups G^♮, N^♮, M^♮.

This page (p.590 in his numbering) opens by finishing that remark: an obvious variant of the proposition gives conditions for φ to extend to S_0 M*_{ρ,σ} → S_0 M^{𝔊'}_{ρ,σ}.

He then starts, and crosses out, a section 'Cas universel'. It takes 𝔊 = GL(2,ℤ)^ (profinite completion) with:
- ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]], of order 6;
- σ = [[0,-1],[1,0]], of order 4;
- τ' = [[0,1],[1,0]] and τ = diag(-1,1), both of determinant -1;
- ε₀ = [[1,-1],[0,1]] and ε₁ = [[1,0],[1,1]], the two unipotent transvections.

One checks:
- ρ³ = σ² = -I.
- σρ = ε₀ and ρσ = ε₁.
- τ'ρτ' = ρ⁻¹ and τστ = σ⁻¹.

So the universal case is the standard presentation SL(2,ℤ) = ⟨ρ,σ | ρ³=σ², σ⁴=1⟩. GL(2,ℤ) is generated by adding an orientation-reversing involution inverting ρ (or σ). The cusp/transvection elements ε₀ and ε₁ appear as the products σρ and ρσ. This is the cartographic setup: 𝔊 = T̂_{1,1}, 𝔊⁺ = SL(2,ℤ)^, with the 'universal' map/dessin group.

The page breaks off at 'Comme ρ'. The section is restarted cleanly on the next page as '8°) Le cas universel'. There he uses the extension 1 → {±1} → M → M_{0,3}~ → 1 to show that M_{0,3}~ injects into Aut(SL(2,ℤ)^).
errors: No mathematical errors. All stated matrices satisfy the intended relations: ρ has order 6, σ has order 4, ρ³ = σ² = -I, σρ = ε₀, ρσ = ε₁, τ' inverts ρ and τ inverts σ.
The first entry of ε₁ is overwritten/illegible in the image; it must be 1 for ε₁ = ρσ to hold, consistent with the evident intent.

ideas.what: Functoriality of the modular groups S_0 M_{ρ,σ} under surjections 𝔊 → 𝔊' (extension conditions for φ to S_0M* → S_0M^{𝔊'})
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of GT-type/automorphism groups of 'cartographic' quotients (characteristic quotients of SL2-hat / Out-groups of dessin groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related work on GT acting on quotients/levels by Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak
ideas.where_published: Only in these manuscript notes (the Esquisse sketches the GT idea without this formalism)

ideas.what: Universal case 𝔊 = GL(2,ℤ)^ with explicit generators ρ (order 6), σ (order 4), reflections τ, τ', transvections ε₀ = σρ, ε₁ = ρσ
ideas.modern_name: Standard presentation of SL(2,ℤ) ≅ ℤ/4 *_{ℤ/2} ℤ/6, the cartographic group of (triangular) maps; profinite completion T̂_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); cartographic group viewpoint: Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984), Malle–Matzat, Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, SL(2,ℤ) and dessins)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short wrap-up remark plus a crossed-out false start of the 'universal case'. It only writes down standard generators of GL(2,ℤ). The substantive content continues on the next page and is in line with known GT/SL2-hat results.
transcription_corrections: The whole 'Cas universel ... Comme ρ' block is struck through by long diagonal strokes, not just marked [-...-] line by line.
The upper-left entry of ε₁ is overwritten (an illegible crossed word 'Ou...' sits above it); intended value is 1, so ε₁ = [[1,0],[1,1]].
Before τ there is a stray brace '{' (", { τ = ..."); before ε₀ there is '; ' with dashes.
The page number written by Grothendieck is not visible here; the archive number 571 is at the bottom. The neighbouring pages carry his numbering 589/590.
First line likely reads 'proposition, fournissant des conditions de prolongement de φ en S₀M*_{ρ,σ} → S₀M^{𝔊'}_{ρ,σ}' (reading uncertain).
